## Introduction

To close this workshop, we look back at the workflow you used,
take questions, and discuss how to apply it in your own work. 

The aim of the session was to experience an end-to-end reproducible research workflow, not to master every package.

## The workflow you used

Each stage recorded something another
researcher needs to understand, rerun, or cite the result.

| Stage | What it recorded | Where to find it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Git and GitHub | Change history and review | Commits and pull requests |
| renv, Docker, Binder | Package versions and computing environment | `renv.lock`, `VERSION`, `outputs/health-wellbeing/session-info.txt`, and the Dockerfiles on GitHub |
| dataspice, rfair | Variable meanings, source and licence, plus evidence from an automated FAIR assessment | `data/metadata/health-wellbeing/dataspice.json` and, if saved, `outputs/health-wellbeing/metadata/fair-assessment.rds` |
| pins, vetiver | Exact input and predictive model versions | `dataset-versions.csv`, `predictive-model-version.txt`, pin metadata |
| targets | The steps from input to summary, and their dependencies | `workspace/_targets.R`, `meta-summary.csv` |
| Quarto | Methods, results, and provenance in one document | `workspace/report.html` |
| GitHub releases, Zenodo | A citable, archived version | Release tag and [concept DOI](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24342489) |

## Discussion {#extras-discussion}

Discuss one or more of these questions with
your neighbours or the room.

-   Which record from today, such as the lockfile, the metadata, the
    data version, or the report's provenance, would have saved time in a
    past project?
-   If the original data could not be shared, what could a reader
    test with a synthetic dataset, and what would require access to
    the originals?
-   Which barrier to reproducibility do you meet most often:
    undocumented dependencies, manual analysis steps, or assumptions
    tied to one computer?
-   Which single change would make your own research workflow easier
    for a collaborator to inspect and rerun?

In the remaining time, we can cover any questions or comments.
